paragraphs: Okay, friend, here's the big idea, and it's a heavy one. The LORD sees everything, and nobody gets out of His sight. Dig down to Sheol, climb up to heaven, hide on top of Carmel or at the bottom of the sea, and the LORD says it's all the same to Him (Amos 9:2-3). That's why this lands so hard on the ones who say, "Disaster will never draw near or confront us" (Amos 9:10).

Now look at what the LORD says to Israel in the middle of it: "Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel?" (Amos 9:7). Being His people was never a free pass. I think that stung, friend. It's like a coupon with no expiration date that turns out to be expired. I would know, I kept one in a drawer for years and it never got me a thing.

But hold on, because the passage doesn't end in the dark. The LORD says, "Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob" (Amos 9:8), and even in the shaking, "not a pebble will reach the ground" (Amos 9:9). So here's what to carry out of the bakery today: don't coast, and don't hide, because the LORD sees you either way. And you can trust Him, because even when He sifts, He keeps hold of what is His. The story isn't over, either, so keep those ovens warm.
